title: IUKA SCHOOL THREAT
full_story:
A student suspect has been identified after a threatening note prompted a lockdown at Iuka Grade School on Tuesday.

Marion County Sheriff Kevin Cripps confirmed that action has been taken against the individual responsible for the note, which contained a potential threat to students inside the building.

Following the discovery of the note, school administrators immediately placed the facility on lockdown.  Responding sheriff’s deputies launched a preliminary investigation, reviewing evidence and conducting interviews that ultimately led them to the suspect.

Deputies also conducted a safety check at the suspect’s residence, verifying that the student does not have access to firearms.  School officials are continuing to follow safety protocols, and the Marion County State’s Attorney’s Office is reviewing the case for potential charges.

Anyone with questions regarding the investigation is asked to contact Lieutenant Anthony Decker at the Marion County Sheriff’s Office.

title: YOUNG HUNTERS SET RECORD
full_story:
Young hunters in Illinois set a new youth deer season harvest record with a preliminary total of 4,852 deer taken October 10th through 12th.  The total surpasses the previous record of 4,714 deer harvested in 2025.

Harvest totals in Clay County were up this year with 105 deer taken as compared to 92 last year.  Other area counties with higher harvest totals include Fayette County where 145 deer were taken compared to 122 last year.  Richland County youth harvested 47 deer compared to 38 last year and Wayne County’s total was 114 compared to 92 last year.

Area counties with lower harvest numbers include Effingham County where the harvest was down to 89 compared to 118 in 2025.  Jasper County with 82, as compared to 97 last year and Marion County where the harvest total was 125 compared to 135.

The top harvest counties were Randolph with 278 deer; Jefferson, 166; Pike, 150; Fayette, 145; and Marion, 125.

Youth hunters with unfilled, valid youth deer permits may use those permits during the upcoming firearm deer seasons November 20th through 22nd and December 3rd through 6th.  This is the first year youth deer hunting permits were sold as a combination that includes one either-sex permit and one antlerless-only permit.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble Village Board of Trustees approved the purchase of new inclusive park equipment and addressed local infrastructure repairs during its regular meeting on Tuesday.

In an effort to improve local park accessibility, the board voted unanimously to purchase an Elite 3.5″ Arch Post Swing system featuring two child adaptive seats.

The board reviewed two separate equipment options before moving forward with the adaptive swing system.  By opting to have village employees handle the equipment installation and choosing to source necessary timbers separately, the village managed to reduce the initial project cost to $4,564.00, yielding an estimated savings of $1,165.00.  Trustee Ashley Pipher noted she is currently researching costs for a heavy-duty rubber mat to further improve playground access for individuals with disabilities.

The board authorized sending a repair invoice to a local customer who failed to contact the JULIE safety system before excavating. The unannounced digging resulted in infrastructure damage that required village labor and materials to fix.  Village Clerk Cindy Manuel will mail an invoice seeking full reimbursement for the repair costs incurred by the village.

Clerk Manuel received approval to attend a two-day billing system training session on October 21st and 22nd in Steeleville.  The classes cost $350.00 in total and due to the 2.5-hour travel distance, Trustee Gary Ulm recommended an overnight stay, and Mayor Brad Kessler approved utilizing the village credit card to cover travel, lodging, and meals.

The annual Halloween Parade at Noble Park is scheduled for Friday, October 30th, beginning with a Cake Walk at 6:30 pm followed by the parade at 7:00 pm.  Official village Trick-or-Treat hours will take place the following evening, Saturday, October 31st, from 6:00 to 8:00 pm.

title: OCC SCIENCE LABS OPEN HOUSE
full_story:
Olney Central College is getting ready to pull back the curtain on a massive upgrade to its campus.

This Tuesday, the college will host a public open house to showcase its newly renovated science labs inside the Dr. Kent L. Wattleworth Hall.  The extensive two-million-dollar project marks the first major overhaul for the third-floor physics, chemistry, and biology facilities since the building first opened in 1974.

School officials say the summer-long renovations replaced obsolete workspaces with modern, high-tech environments.  Faculty members note that the upgrades don’t just solve decades-old infrastructure problems like plumbing leaks and power outages, they also introduce advanced safety equipment, dual chemical hoods, and a dedicated space for the college’s anatomy cadaver.

OCC President Chris Simpson says the new facilities will drastically enhance student success, giving them access to undergraduate research projects that rival major universities.

The project was heavily backed by the OCC Foundation, which contributed thousands of dollars in equipment, including a new ten-thousand-dollar water purification system.

The open house runs Tuesday from 4:00 to 6:00 pm, and community members, alumni, and prospective students are all invited to attend.

title: CITY OF FLORA ANNOUNCEMENTS
full_story:
The Flora Public Library will be closed until further notice due to major leaks in the library. The library thanks all of the city workers who came in and helped getting everything covered. The library apologizes for any inconvenience.

The City of Flora has also postponed the closing of Charlie Brown Park to Monday and Tuesday of next week due to recent rains.

Campers will be able to access the rear entrance to campsites only, the rest of park will be closed.  Golfers are advised to use the Country Club’s west entrance off of Country Club Road during these times as the east entrance will be blocked off.  The City apologizes for the inconvenience.  There will also be temporary intermittent closures across town these two days as well for some spot patching and oiling as well.

title: ISP STOLEN VEHICLE DETAIL
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) continues to target vehicle theft, hijacking, and related violent crimes using grant funding from the Illinois Secretary of State Illinois Vehicle Hijacking and Motor Vehicle Theft Prevention and Insurance Verification Council.  ISP was awarded a $10 million grant for the first fiscal year, another $677,000 in June 2024, and $637,500 in July 2025.

From July through September, ISP missions resulted in 424 vehicles recovered, 21 stolen vehicles arrested, 1 hijacked vehicle arrest, 7 firearms seized, and 1,146 forensic laboratory assignments related to stolen vehicles.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Illinois harvest progress, much like the weather, heated up recently as farmers combined 17% of soybeans and 15% of the corn crop statewide in one week.

According to the USDA there were 6.4 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending October 11th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 64.1 degrees, 6 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.05 inches, 0.66 inches below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 13% very short, 28% short, 54% adequate, and 5% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 13% very short, 29% short, 53% adequate, and 5% surplus.

Corn mature reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 94%.  Corn harvested reached 51%, compared to the 5-year average of 44%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 14% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 93%, compared to the 5-year average of 94%.  Soybeans harvested reached 48%, compared to the 5-year average of 46%.  Soybeans condition was rated 3% very poor, 7% poor, 30% fair, 47% good, and 13% excellent.

Winter wheat planted reached 28%, compared to the 5-year average of 29%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 5%, compared to the 5-year average of 10%.

title: CONFIRMED MOUNTAIN LIONS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) recently confirmed a large cat spotted in Union and Jackson counties on multiple occasions between August and September was a mountain lion.  Both sightings are believed to be the same animal.  It is the 12th confirmed mountain lion in Illinois since 2002 and first since 2025 in Pike County.

Mountain lions, also known as cougars or pumas, have a tan or tawny coat and a white or cream-colored chin, undersides and inside of legs.  The ears are rounded and the back of the ears are solid black to dark gray.

“If you see a mountain lion, do not run.  Do not surprise the mountain lion.  Make noise to ensure the animal is aware of your presence,” IDNR noted.  “Respect the mountain lion’s space and do not approach the animal.”

Mountain lions have been protected in Illinois since 2015.  Mountain lions may not be hunted, killed or harassed unless there is an imminent threat to a person or property.

To report a mountain lion sighting or learn about options available to address potential threats, contact the IDNR.

title: CARLYLE LAKE EVENTS
full_story:
Carlyle Lake will host several public events this fall in partnership with local organizations.  The following events are scheduled at various locations around the lake.

The Carlyle Lake Haunted Trail will be held on tomorrow and Saturday at the Dam West Boat Ramp from 6:30–10 pm each evening.  Participants will take a hayride from the boat ramp down to the Little Prairie Nature Trail, a 1/2-mile trail featuring spooky displays and plenty of Halloween thrills.  Admission is $15.  Proceeds will support the 2027 Fireworks Spectacular.

And the Camper’s & Family Trick-or-Treat will be held on October 24th at Dam West Campground from 6:30 to 8 pm.  Dam West Campground will host a Halloween-themed evening featuring trick-or-treating and a campsite decorating contest.  The event is open to friends and family of registered campers.  Proper identification is required.

For additional information, contact the Carlyle Lake Project Office at (618) 594-2484 or [email protected]. Information is also available on the official Carlyle Lake Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/carlylelake.
